name: Reptile House
label: Dischord
lede: Baltimore's hardcore band with a psychedelic streak: a singer who'd become Daniel Higgs, a drummer bound for Samhain, and four songs from Inner Ear that sat out of print for a quarter century.

eras.title: Baltimore, from scratch
eras.text: D.C. had Dischord and a scene with a name. Baltimore, forty miles up the road, had a few clubs like the Marble Bar and Jules Club House and a handful of kids. Reptile House, per AllMusic, became the city's leading hardcore band, mixing D.C. drive and California punk with darker imagery and psychedelic guitar.

years.h: Joe Goldsborough and Daniel Strasser start Reptile House
years.p: High school friends [[Joe Goldsborough|279792ca-9410-4c9c-96e9-aad841c43f05]], on guitar, and singer Daniel V. Strasser, later [[Daniel Higgs|6dd4abcc-0321-4ac0-b3bf-0a9422c450d9]], form Reptile House. AllMusic's original lineup adds David Rhodes on bass and [[London May|57e0394c-afeb-4021-8193-940084dd4717]] on drums.

years.h: Reptile House's first record: a flexi in Testube zine
years.p: Two Reptile House songs on a self-released flexi-disc tucked into Testube zine, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Maryland Center for History and Culture
years.h: Reptile House at the New Loft, on the front page of the Sun
years.p: At the New Loft on Mulberry and Eutaw, Joseph Kohl photographs Reptile House singer Daniel Strasser sharing the mic with a kid in the crowd, Anthony "Toad" Brennan, while Joe Goldsborough plays guitar.
years.xp: The Maryland Center for History and Culture dates Joseph Kohl's photo to about 1984, possibly November 2. Scene regular Skizz Cyzyk later said the picture ran a full front page in The Baltimore Sun. For a confrontational hardcore scene that mainstream papers mostly ignored, that was rare.

eras.title: Four songs, two labels
eras.text: Reptile House drove down to Arlington to make their first real record, 4-Songs, with Ian MacKaye producing. It came out as a split release between Dischord and the band's own Druid Hill label.

years.h: Reptile House drummer London May joins Glenn Danzig's Samhain
years.p: London May joins [[Samhain|7991397c-2baf-49f3-8d73-c78e428825f8]], Glenn Danzig's post-[[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] band, in 1985 and plays on November-Coming-Fire. Gary Breezee is later listed on Reptile House's drum stool.

years.src: Dischord · Maryland Center for History and Culture
years.h: 4-Songs, Reptile House's debut 7" · Dischord / Druid Hill
years.p: Recorded at Inner Ear in March 1985 with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] engineering, it came out in November on Dischord and the band's own Druid Hill label. Collectors know it as I Stumble as the Crow Flies.
years.xp: The four songs are Keel Haul Love, Social Champion, Mrs. Rain and Sleestak Weather, with [[Leigh Panlilio|b24853ba-d025-4da6-b30f-5d1d5b09498b]] now on bass. London May has compared the sound to [[Flipper|4e99b3a5-654b-43ee-a9bf-c55c155c0495]]: mid-tempo rhythms and a noisy, jam-session feel, according to Wikipedia's account of his interviews.

eras.title: Detroit, Texas and the Powersoul
eras.text: Reptile House went on the road, touring as far as Detroit and Texas per AllMusic, and headlined D.C.'s 9:30 Club. By the end Asa Osborne was in on guitar, Listen to the Powersoul was out on Joe Goldsborough's Merkin label, and singer Daniel Strasser was about to become Daniel Higgs.

years.p: Dischord notes later Reptile House lineups included Asa Osborne on guitar, the start of his partnership with singer Daniel Strasser, later Daniel Higgs, that would outlast the band.

years.h: Listen to the Powersoul, Reptile House's only album · Merkin
years.p: Reptile House's only album, released on guitarist Joe Goldsborough's Merkin Records in fall 1988.

years.h: Daniel Strasser becomes Daniel Higgs and starts [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]]
years.p: Shortly after Listen to the Powersoul, singer Daniel Strasser leaves Reptile House, takes the surname Higgs, and forms Lungfish with Asa Osborne. Reptile House recruits ex-Grey March keyboardist Ron Weldon to sing, then breaks up soon after.

years.h: Joe Goldsborough forms the Ultra Violets, keeps Merkin going
years.p: Reptile House guitarist Joe Goldsborough forms the psychedelic pop band the Ultra Violets with Reptile House bassist Joey Cirri, and uses his Merkin label to document the Baltimore underground into the '90s.

eras.title: Twenty-five years later
eras.text: By 2010 Daniel Higgs had spent two decades fronting Lungfish on Dischord. The label brought the first Reptile House record, 4-Songs, back for its 25th anniversary.

years.p: After years out of print, Reptile House's 1985 7" returns as Dischord 15.75, announced alongside reissues from Dag Nasty, Artificial Peace and Government Issue. Wikipedia notes it has never been on CD in its original form.
Ex-Reptile House guitarist Joe Goldsborough joins Gag School with Kenny Sanders, Ken Mosher and Joe LaVoie, per Wikipedia.
